segments.text: Today we interview a researcher working on retrieval augmented generation.
He explains that RAG grounds a language model in retrieved documents.
The retriever finds relevant passages and the generator writes the answer.
He says the biggest quality lever is retrieval, not the generator.
If the right passage is missing the model will hallucinate confidently.
He measures retrieval with recall at k before touching the prompt.
For chunking he prefers semantic boundaries over fixed token windows.
Overlapping chunks help when an answer spans a boundary.
He warns that long context windows do not remove the need for retrieval.
Feeding everything into context is expensive and dilutes attention.
For evaluation he uses a labeled set with gold supporting passages.
He also tracks citation accuracy so answers point to real evidence.
On languages he notes cross lingual retrieval is still an open challenge.
His parting advice is to instrument retrieval before optimizing the model.
